history.period: CONFLICT (verify): ASI/Bihar State Religious Trust Board claim 108 CE (30th year of Saka era); historians date the existing sculptures and architecture to 6th-7th century, and the present octagonal shrine may be 16th-17th century rebuilding incorporating older elements
history.summary: The Mundeshwari Devi Temple at Ramgarh village on the Mundeshwari Hills of the Kaimur plateau is an ASI-protected monument (since 1915) dedicated to Devi Mundeshwari (a tantric form of Durga) and Shiva. It is claimed as the world's oldest functional Hindu temple, with unbroken worship and an inscriptional tradition going back to at least 635 CE (site plaque); palaeographers place the Udayasena inscription c. 570-590 CE, and architectural historians date most fabric to the 6th-7th century, with the current octagonal shrine possibly 16th-17th century. Finds include a Brahmi seal of Sri Lankan king Dutthagamani (1st century BCE), suggesting an ancient pilgrim centre; Huen Tsang (636-638 CE) described a shining hilltop shrine here. The temple is famous for its bloodless tantric goat 'sacrifice' ritual and the colour-changing Panchmukhi Shivalinga in the sanctum. CSV town 'Mundeshwari' corrected to Ramgarh village (near Bhagwanpur/Bhabua, Kaimur district).

name: Mundeshwari Devi Temple
town_description: Ramgarh is a village at the foot of the Mundeshwari Hills on the Kaimur plateau in Kaimur (Bhabua) district, southwestern Bihar, near the Son river. It is the base for the ancient Mundeshwari hilltop shrine, now developed with roads, stairs, resting areas and an eco-park. The nearest towns are Bhabua (district HQ) and Mohania, with rail and road links toward Varanasi and Patna.

travel.airport: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi, ~102 km
travel.railway: Mohania - Bhabua Road railway station, ~22 km by road
travel.road: Reachable by road via Patna, Gaya or Varanasi; the hilltop is now served by roads and stairs with public amenities

visitor_information.best_time: October-March for weather; Ramnavami, Shivratri and Navaratra for the mela (very crowded)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opens half an hour before sunrise and closes at sunset; break noon-12:20 pm; Manokamana aarti 11:30 am-12 pm; Shringar aarti half an hour before sunset (verify). Entry free; VIP darshan Rs 501 (verify).
